statement: Find the reflection $Q$ of the point $P(2,3)$ in the line $3x+4y-5=0$, and verify that the midpoint of $PQ$ lies on the line.
solution: For a line $ax+by+c=0$ the reflection of $(x_{0},y_{0})$ is $(x_{0},y_{0})-2\dfrac{ax_{0}+by_{0}+c}{a^{2}+b^{2}}(a,b)$. Here $a=3,b=4,c=-5$ and $ax_{0}+by_{0}+c=6+12-5=13$, $a^{2}+b^{2}=25$. So $Q=(2,3)-\dfrac{26}{25}(3,4)=\left(2-\dfrac{78}{25},\,3-\dfrac{104}{25}\right)=\left(-\dfrac{28}{25},-\dfrac{29}{25}\right)$. Midpoint $M=\left(\dfrac{11}{25},\dfrac{23}{25}\right)$ and $3\cdot\tfrac{11}{25}+4\cdot\tfrac{23}{25}-5=\tfrac{33+92-125}{25}=0$, so $M$ lies on the line.
hints: Use the reflection formula involving the line's normal.
Check that the midpoint satisfies the line equation.
